info.title: Magna Carta API
info.description: The Magna Carta legal practice-management API. Every operation is enforced at one chokepoint (tenancy → authn → RBAC → idempotency → rate-limit); errors are RFC 9457 problem documents.

get.description: Service health — the walking-skeleton control-plane round trip.
The session user, their firm, and their effective permissions — the SPA's bootstrap call.

200.description: The session user, firm, and effective permissions

404.description: The session's firm is not reachable from this deployment, or the session user is a deactivated member of it (absent, never an existence oracle)

get.description: The firm's own usage: storage consumed (by class) and entity counts (matters by status, files, versions, folders, locations).

403.description: Authenticated, but the member lacks tools:firmUsage

post.description: Invites a member into the session firm: creates the (unverified, account-less) user, enqueues the per-firm member.provision outbox row, audits the invite — one atomic batch — then sends the activation email (a password-reset link; the reset creates the credential).

201.description: The invited user, pending activation through the emailed reset link

post.description: Provisions a tenant firm (platform-admin only): firm row, per-firm database created and migrated to head, bucket, owner user with the Owner/Admin role — resumable; re-invoking with the same name no-ops completed steps and returns the existing firm.

201.description: The provisioned (or, on an idempotent re-invoke, existing) active firm

409.description: An active firm already holds this name with a different owner, a request with this Idempotency-Key is still in progress, or a concurrent provisioning of the same name completed first (retry to observe it)

422.description: The owner email already belongs to another user, or the Idempotency-Key was reused with a different payload

post.description: Files a diagnostic incident from the session firm: writes the per-firm incident row and the incident.created outbox row in one atomic batch (the diagnostics agent's future feed). Any member may report; the description is the user's words, the rest is id-and-action shaped.

post.description: Begins a direct-to-R2 upload: mints the pending file/version/upload-session rows and returns either a single-shot presigned PUT (at or below the firm's mode threshold) or a multipart session (above it). The bytes never transit the Worker.

get.description: Resolves the file's current clean version and redirects (302) to a short-TTL presigned GET URL the client downloads the bytes directly from. 404 when the file has no clean current version. When a re-scan has flagged the current version as malware, the file stays accessible (no data loss) but the raw download is gated: a 409 carrying the signature unless the caller re-requests with acknowledgeMalware=true, which proceeds and is audited as an acknowledged override.

302.description: Redirect to the presigned download URL

404.description: The firm is unreachable, the member is deactivated, or the file is unknown

409.description: The current version was flagged as malware; re-request with acknowledgeMalware=true to download it

get.description: Authorizes inline preview of the file's current clean version and returns a delivery descriptor. When the verdict + storage facts permit inline media, the descriptor carries a short-lived signed streamUrl on the cookieless files host the player loads as a <video>/<audio> subresource; otherwise it carries download-only with a reason. downloadUrl (the audited download path) is always present. Untrusted bytes are served cookieless so a malicious file reaches only the media decoder, never a privileged origin. 404 when the file has no clean current version.

404.description: The firm is unreachable, the member is deactivated, or the file is unknown

post.description: Resolves a selection of folders and/or files within a matter to their current clean versions at request time, then streams a ZIP of those bytes (entry paths follow the folder tree). A selection that resolves to a single file redirects (302) to a presigned download instead. An empty selection (matter only) bundles the whole matter.

200.description: A streamed ZIP archive of the selected files; or, when the selection exceeds the live threshold and an identical bundle was already built, a JSON body with a fresh signed URL.

202.description: The selection exceeds the live-download threshold; a background build was started or is already in progress. Poll the bundle-status endpoint with the returned jobId.

302.description: A single-file selection redirects to a presigned download URL

403.description: The session member lacks files:organize

404.description: The firm is unreachable, the member is deactivated, or the selection is empty

post.description: Scans an uploaded file — the raw bytes as the application/octet-stream request body — through the malware-scan engine and returns its verdict + details. A one-off diagnostic: the file is NOT stored and is NOT associated with any matter. Returns an honest `unscanned` verdict until the scan Container is activated (the engine-less adapter never reports a false `clean`).

413.description: The body exceeds the firm's inspectable-size cap

get.description: Reports the state of an async bulk-download build (building, ready, or failed). A ready job carries a freshly minted, short-lived signed URL to the built ZIP artifact.
